Glossary of astronomy.fact: galactic astronomy The branch of astronomy that studies objects and phenomena within the Milky Way galaxy, as opposed to everything outside of the Milky Way, which is the domain of extragalactic astronomy. galactic anticenter The direction in space that is directly opposite the center of the Milky Way Galaxy, as viewed from Earth; considered as a point on the celestial sphere, the Milky Way's anticenter is in the constellation Auriga.

Glossary of astronomy.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of astronomy.question: The Solar System is located on the inner edge of one of the _____'s spiral arms, about 27,000 light-years from the Galactic Center, which the Sun orbits with a period of 240 million years
Glossary of astronomy.fact: The Milky Way Galaxy has a diameter of 100,000–200,000 light-years and is estimated to contain 100–400 billion stars and at least that number of planets. The Solar System is located on the inner edge of one of the Milky Way's spiral arms, about 27,000 light-years from the Galactic Center, which the Sun orbits with a period of 240 million years.

Glossary of astronomy.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of astronomy.question: In 1953, after some revisions to the list of standard stars and classification criteria, the scheme was named the _____–Keenan classification, or MK, which remains in use today
Glossary of astronomy.fact: It was introduced in 1943 by William Wilson Morgan, Philip C. Keenan, and Edith Kellman from Yerkes Observatory. In 1953, after some revisions to the list of standard stars and classification criteria, the scheme was named the Morgan–Keenan classification, or MK, which remains in use today.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.fact: acclimatization (physiology) Adaptation to a new climate, as with a new temperature or altitude or environment.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.fact: aerobic Capable of surviving and growing in the presence of oxygen.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.fact: autotroph Sometimes used interchangeably with primary producer.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.fact: biodiversity A contraction of "biological diversity" generally referring to the variety and variability of life on Earth.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: biomass _____ matter derived from living or recently living organisms
Glossary of biology.fact: biomass Organic matter derived from living or recently living organisms.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: biome Any very large ecological area on the _____'s surface containing fauna and flora (animals and plants) adapting to their environment

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: cell plate _____ in the cell's center, it fuses with the parental plasma membrane, creating a new cell wall that enables cell division

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.fact: cilia circadian rhythm citric acid cycle Also called the Krebs cycle and tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA).

Glossary of biology.fact: In addition, the cycle provides the chemical precursors for certain amino acids as well as the reducing agent NADH that is used in numerous other biochemical reactions.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: Many organisms, such as bacteria, insects, and _____, are capable of naturally producing clones through asexual reproduction
Glossary of biology.fact: Many organisms, such as bacteria, insects, and plants, are capable of naturally producing clones through asexual reproduction.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: cryobiology The branch of biology that studies the effects of low temperatures on living things within _____'s cryosphere or in laboratory experiments
Glossary of biology.fact: cryobiology The branch of biology that studies the effects of low temperatures on living things within Earth's cryosphere or in laboratory experiments.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: It is an interdisciplinary field that combines concepts from biology, geography, and _____ science
Glossary of biology.fact: It is an interdisciplinary field that combines concepts from biology, geography, and Earth science.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.fact: ecotype Sometimes called an ecospecies.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: efferent _____ or conducting outwards or away from something (for nerves, the central nervous system; for blood vessels, the organ supplied)
Glossary of biology.fact: efferent Conducted or conducting outwards or away from something (for nerves, the central nervous system; for blood vessels, the organ supplied).

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.fact: invertebrate A group of animals that have no backbone, unlike animals such as reptiles, amphibians, fish, birds, and mammals, which all have a backbone.

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of biology.question: exogenous (of a substance or process) _____ outside of or external to a system (such as an organism, tissue, or cell), as with drugs and many pathogens

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of biology.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: The hypothetical electric charge (positive, negative, or zero) that an atom would have if all bonds to atoms of different elements were 100% ionic, with no covalent component.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: pentabasic (of a chemical compound) _____ five hydrogen atoms which may be replaced by metals or bases
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: pentabasic (of a chemical compound) Having five hydrogen atoms which may be replaced by metals or bases.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: per- A prefix in _____ chemical nomenclature meaning complete, exhaustive, or extreme, as in a completely substituted hydrocarbon; or indicating the presence of a peroxy group
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: per- A prefix in IUPAC chemical nomenclature meaning complete, exhaustive, or extreme, as in a completely substituted hydrocarbon; or indicating the presence of a peroxy group.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: The first periodic table of the elements was published by Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in _____
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: The first periodic table of the elements was published by Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: Plasma does not exist freely on the _____'s surface under natural conditions
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: Plasma does not exist freely on the Earth's surface under natural conditions.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: polarity polyatomic Composed of two or more atoms, of the same or different elements. polyatomic ion A molecule composed of two or more covalently bonded atoms which collectively bear a net electric charge and therefore act as an ion.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: (of a chemical species) _____ of acting as a proton donor; readily generating or yielding free protons (H+) in solution
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: (of a chemical species) Capable of acting as a proton donor; readily generating or yielding free protons (H+) in solution.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: Protic species may therefore be considered strongly or weakly acidic in the sense of a Brønsted–_____ acid
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: Protic species may therefore be considered strongly or weakly acidic in the sense of a Brønsted–Lowry acid.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: radiation _____ released in the form of waves or subatomic particles when there is a change from high-energy to low-energy states
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: radiation Energy released in the form of waves or subatomic particles when there is a change from high-energy to low-energy states.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: reactant _____ used interchangeably with reagent
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: reactant Sometimes used interchangeably with reagent.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: saturation _____ödinger equation A quantum state equation which represents the behaviour of an electron around an atom
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: saturation Schrödinger equation A quantum state equation which represents the behaviour of an electron around an atom.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: Such interactions generally involve electrostatic forces and van der _____ forces, as well as compound-specific effects such as hydrogen bonding
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: Such interactions generally involve electrostatic forces and van der Waals forces, as well as compound-specific effects such as hydrogen bonding.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: Standard temperature is 25 degrees _____ (°C) and standard pressure is 100.000 kilopascals (kPa)
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: Standard temperature is 25 degrees Celsius (°C) and standard pressure is 100.000 kilopascals (kPa).

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: Standard conditions are often denoted with the abbreviation STP or _____
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: Standard conditions are often denoted with the abbreviation STP or SATP.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: uncertainty principle _____ the location of a particle makes the momentum uncertain, while knowing the momentum of a particle makes the location uncertain
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: uncertainty principle Knowing the location of a particle makes the momentum uncertain, while knowing the momentum of a particle makes the location uncertain.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: unit factor _____ used in converting between units
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: unit factor Statements used in converting between units.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: van der _____ force One of the forces (attraction/repulsion) between molecules
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: van der Waals force One of the forces (attraction/repulsion) between molecules.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: van 't _____ factor The ratio of moles of particles in solution to moles of solute dissolved
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: van 't Hoff factor The ratio of moles of particles in solution to moles of solute dissolved.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: It is the most abundant substance on _____ and therefore an integral component of virtually all chemical and biological systems
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: water A polar inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O that is a tasteless, odorless, and generally colorless liquid at standard temperature and pressure, though it also occurs naturally as a solid and a gas at the Earth's surface. It is the most abundant substance on Earth and therefore an integral component of virtually all chemical and biological systems.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: manometer An instrument used to measure pressure invented by _____ in 1643
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: manometer An instrument used to measure pressure invented by Evangelista Torricelli in 1643.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: The first periodic table of the elements was published by Russian chemist _____ in 1869
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: The first periodic table of the elements was published by Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.

Glossary of chemistry terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of chemistry terms.question: Molarity is typically expressed in units of moles per litre (mol/L); a solution with a concentration of exactly 1 mol/L is commonly said to be 1 molar, abbreviated 1 M. _____ molality
Glossary of chemistry terms.fact: Molarity is typically expressed in units of moles per litre (mol/L); a solution with a concentration of exactly 1 mol/L is commonly said to be 1 molar, abbreviated 1 M. Contrast molality.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: The _____ was List of definitions of terms and concepts related to civil engineering.
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: This glossary of civil engineering terms is a list of definitions of terms and concepts pertaining specifically to civil engineering, its sub-disciplines, and related fields.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: It can be used as a hand-held instrument or mounted on a _____'s staff for more precise measurement

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of civil engineering.fact: Abrams' law Also Abrams' water-cement ratio law.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: The corresponding Kelvin and _____ temperature scales set their zero points at absolute zero by definition
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: The corresponding Kelvin and Rankine temperature scales set their zero points at absolute zero by definition.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: acid A molecule or ion capable of donating a hydron (proton or hydrogen ion H+), or, alternatively, capable of forming a covalent bond with an electron pair (a _____ acid)

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: The research in this area is coordinated by a task group of the _____ (IWA)
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: The research in this area is coordinated by a task group of the International Water Association (IWA).

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: amino acid A class of organic compound containing amine (-NH2) and carboxyl (-_____) functional groups, along with a side chain (R group) specific to each amino acid
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: amino acid A class of organic compound containing amine (-NH2) and carboxyl (-COOH) functional groups, along with a side chain (R group) specific to each amino acid.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: ampere often shortened to "amp", is the base unit of electric current in the _____ of Units (SI)
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: ampere often shortened to "amp", is the base unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: It is named after André-Marie Ampère (_____–1836), French mathematician and physicist, considered the father of electrodynamics
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: It is named after André-Marie Ampère (1775–1836), French mathematician and physicist, considered the father of electrodynamics.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of civil engineering.fact: In SI units, it is measured in radians per second squared (rad/s2), and is usually denoted by the Greek letter alpha (α).

Glossary of civil engineering.fact: annealing anode ANSI Archimedes' principle states that the upward buoyant force that is exerted on a body immersed in a fluid, whether fully or partially submerged, is equal to the weight of the fluid that the body displaces and acts in the upward direction at the center of mass of the displaced fluid. Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: It is one of three standard moduli used to describe a material's response to stress, along with the shear modulus and _____'s modulus
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: It is one of three standard moduli used to describe a material's response to stress, along with the shear modulus and Young's modulus.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: In much of the world the utility frequency is standardized at 50 Hz, although in the _____ and parts of Asia it is typically 60 Hz
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: In much of the world the utility frequency is standardized at 50 Hz, although in the Americas and parts of Asia it is typically 60 Hz.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of civil engineering.question: zeroth law of thermodynamics _____ that if two thermodynamic systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third one, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other
Glossary of civil engineering.fact: zeroth law of thermodynamics States that if two thermodynamic systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third one, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.

Glossary of civil engineering.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of civil engineering.fact: This empirical law was first observed by John Dalton in 1801 and published in 1802, and is closely related to the ideal gas laws.

Glossary of clinical research.fact: The phrase "responses to a medicinal product" means that a causal relationship between a medicinal product and an adverse event is at least a reasonable possibility, i.e., the relationship cannot be ruled out. Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ reaction An unwanted effect caused by the administration of drugs
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Adverse events do not have to be caused by the drug or therapy, and they may be mild, moderate, or severe. (ICH E6) Adverse reaction An unwanted effect caused by the administration of drugs.

Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ study A laboratory experiment using animals to study the development and progression of diseases
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Animal model An animal with a disease either the same as or like a disease in humans. Animal models are used to study the development and progression of diseases and to test new treatments before they are given to humans.

Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ drugs In the U.S., the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) must approve a substance as a drug before it can be marketed
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Approved drugs In the U.S., the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) must approve a substance as a drug before it can be marketed.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ practice In medicine, treatment that experts agree is appropriate, accepted, and widely used
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Best practice In medicine, treatment that experts agree is appropriate, accepted, and widely used. Health care providers are obligated to provide patients with the best practice.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ a scientific research study or clinical trial, a flaw in the study design or the method of collecting or interpreting information
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Bias In a scientific research study or clinical trial, a flaw in the study design or the method of collecting or interpreting information.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ ability of a drug or other substance to be absorbed and used by the body
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Bioavailable The ability of a drug or other substance to be absorbed and used by the body.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ science of using computers, databases, and math to organize and analyze large amounts of biological, medical, and health information
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Bioinformatics The science of using computers, databases, and math to organize and analyze large amounts of biological, medical, and health information.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ drug A substance that is made from a living organism or its products and is used in the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment diseases
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Bioinformatics The science of using computers, databases, and math to organize and analyze large amounts of biological, medical, and health information. (NCI) Biological drug A substance that is made from a living organism or its products and is used in the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment diseases.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ science of collecting and analyzing biologic or health data using statistical methods
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Biometrics The science of collecting and analyzing biologic or health data using statistical methods.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ A randomized trial is "Blind" if the participant is not told which arm of the trial he is on
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Blind A randomized trial is "Blind" if the participant is not told which arm of the trial he is on. A clinical trial is "Blind" if participants are unaware on whether they are in the experimental or control arm of the study; also called masked.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: A clinical trial is "_____" if participants are unaware on whether they are in the experimental or control arm of the study; also called masked
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Blind A randomized trial is "Blind" if the participant is not told which arm of the trial he is on. A clinical trial is "Blind" if participants are unaware on whether they are in the experimental or control arm of the study; also called masked.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ study A type of study in which the patients (single-blinded) or the patients and their doctors (double-blinded) do not know which drug or treatment is being given
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Blinded study A type of study in which the patients (single-blinded) or the patients and their doctors (double-blinded) do not know which drug or treatment is being given. The opposite of a blinded study is an open label study.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ report form A printed, optical, or electronic document designed to record all of the protocol-required information to be reported to the sponsor on each trial subject
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Case report A detailed report of the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of an individual patient. Case reports also contain some demographic information about the patient (for example, age, gender, ethnic origin).

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ series A group or series of case reports involving patients who were given similar treatment
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Case report A detailed report of the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of an individual patient. Case reports also contain some demographic information about the patient (for example, age, gender, ethnic origin).

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ to or founded on observation and treatment of participants, as distinguished from theoretical or basic science
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Clinical Pertaining to or set up on observation and treatment of participants, as distinguished from theoretical or basic science.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) Clinical practice guidelines _____ developed to help health care professionals and patients make decisions about screening, prevention, or treatment of a specific health condition
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Clinical practice guidelines Guidelines developed to help health care professionals and patients make decisions about screening, prevention, or treatment of a specific health condition.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ A health professional who takes care of patients
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Clinician A health professional who takes care of patients.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ (statistics) A group of individuals who share a common trait, such as birth year
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Cohort (statistics) A group of individuals who share a common trait, such as birth year. In medicine, a cohort is a group that is part of a clinical trial or study and is observed over a period of time.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____-based clinical trial (CBCT) A clinical trial conducted primarily through primary-care physicians rather than academic research facilities
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Community-based clinical trial (CBCT) A clinical trial conducted primarily through primary-care physicians rather than academic research facilities.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Comparator An investigational or marketed product (i.e., active control), or placebo, used as a reference in a clinical trial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ use A method of providing experimental therapeutics prior to final FDA approval for use in humans
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Compassionate use A method of providing experimental therapeutics prior to final FDA approval for use in humans. Often, case-by-case approval must be obtained from the FDA for "compassionate use" of a drug or therapy.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ to all the trial-related requirements, good clinical practice (GCP) requirements, and the applicable regulatory requirements
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Compliance Adherence to all the trial-related requirements, good clinical practice (GCP) requirements, and the applicable regulatory requirements.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ regarding trial participants Refers to maintaining the confidentiality of trial participants including their personal identity and all personal medical information
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Confidentiality regarding trial participants Refers to maintaining the confidentiality of trial participants including their personal identity and all personal medical information. The trial participants' consent to the use of records for data verification purposes should be obtained prior to the trial and assurance must be given that confidentiality will be maintained.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ of disclosure, to other than authorized individuals, of a sponsor's proprietary information or of a subject's identity
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Prevention of disclosure, to other than authorized individuals, of a sponsor's proprietary information or of a subject's identity.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ case series A clinical study that includes all eligible patients identified by the researchers during the study registration period
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Consecutive case series A clinical study that includes all eligible patients identified by the researchers during the study registration period.

Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Contract Research Organization A person or an organization (commercial, academic, or other) contracted by the sponsor to perform one or more of a sponsor's trial-related duties and functions.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ A specific circumstance when the use of certain treatments could be harmful
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Contraindication A specific circumstance when the use of certain treatments could be harmful.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Control A control is the nature of the intervention control. (NLM) Control animal An animal in a study that does not receive the treatment being tested.

Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Control A control is the nature of the intervention control. (NLM) Control animal An animal in a study that does not receive the treatment being tested.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
