Glossary of clinical research.fact: A DSMB may recommend that a trial be stopped if there are safety concerns or if the trial objectives have been achieved.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6 and ICH E9) _____ trials Refers to trials that are conducted to find better tests or procedures for diagnosing a particular disease or condition
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6 and ICH E9) Diagnostic trials Refers to trials that are conducted to find better tests or procedures for diagnosing a particular disease or condition. Diagnostic trials usually include people who have signs or symptoms of the disease or condition being studied.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ to examine, analyze, verify, and reproduce any records and reports that are important to evaluation of a clinical trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Direct Access Permission to examine, analyze, verify, and reproduce any records and reports that are important to evaluation of a clinical trial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ amount of medicine taken, or radiation given, at one time
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Dose The amount of medicine taken, or radiation given, at one time.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) Dose-dependent _____ to the effects of treatment with a drug
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Dose-dependent Refers to the effects of treatment with a drug.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) Dose-limiting _____ side effects of a drug or other treatment that are serious enough to prevent an increase in dose or level of that treatment
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Dose-limiting Describes side effects of a drug or other treatment that are serious enough to prevent an increase in dose or level of that treatment.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____-ranging study A clinical trial in which two or more doses of an agent (such as a drug) are tested against each other to determine which dose works best and is least harmful
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Dose-dependent Refers to the effects of treatment with a drug. If the effects change when the dose of the drug is changed, the effects are said to be dose-dependent.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____-rate The strength of a treatment given over a period of time
Glossary of clinical research.fact: If the effects change when the dose of the drug is changed, the effects are said to be dose-dependent. (NCI) Dose-limiting Describes side effects of a drug or other treatment that are serious enough to prevent an increase in dose or level of that treatment.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____-dummy A technique for retaining the blind when administering supplies in a clinical trial, when the two treatments cannot be made identical
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Double-blind study A clinical trial design in which neither the participating individuals nor the study staff knows which participants are receiving the experimental drug and which are receiving a placebo (or another therapy). Double-blind trials are thought to produce objective results, since the expectations of the doctor and the participant about the experimental drug do not affect the outcome; also called double-masked study.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: Supplies are prepared for _____ A (active and indistinguishable placebo) and for Treatment B (active and indistinguishable placebo)
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Double-dummy A technique for retaining the blind when administering supplies in a clinical trial, when the two treatments cannot be made identical. Supplies are prepared for Treatment A (active and indistinguishable placebo) and for Treatment B (active and indistinguishable placebo).

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ A subject in a clinical trial who for any reason fails to continue in the trial until the last visit required of him/her by the study protocol
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Dropout A subject in a clinical trial who for any reason fails to continue in the trial until the last visit required of him/her by the study protocol.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ substance, other than food, that is used to prevent, diagnose, treat or relieve symptoms of a disease or abnormal condition
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Drug Any substance, other than food, that is used to prevent, diagnose, treat or relieve symptoms of a disease or abnormal condition.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____–drug interaction A modification of the effect of a drug when administered with another drug
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Drug Any substance, other than food, that is used to prevent, diagnose, treat or relieve symptoms of a disease or abnormal condition. (NCI) Drug–drug interaction A modification of the effect of a drug when administered with another drug.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: In the procedure mandated by the FDA, Phase II clinical trials gauge efficacy, and Phase III trials confirm it (NLM) _____
Glossary of clinical research.fact: In the procedure mandated by the FDA, Phase II clinical trials gauge efficacy, and Phase III trials confirm it (NLM) Effectiveness.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ criteria In clinical trials, requirements that must be met for an individual to be included in a study
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Eligibility criteria In clinical trials, requirements that must be met for an individual to be included in a study. When all participants meet the same eligibility criteria, it gives researchers greater confidence that results of the study are caused by the intervention being tested and not by other factors.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ criteria for participant selection; includes Inclusion and Exclusion criteria
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Summary criteria for participant selection; includes Inclusion and Exclusion criteria.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ on experimental data, not on a theory
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Empirical Based on experimental data, not on a theory.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ clinical trials, an event or outcome that can be measured objectively to determine whether the intervention being studied is beneficial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Endpoint In clinical trials, an event or outcome that can be measured objectively to determine whether the intervention being studied is beneficial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ outcome that the protocol is designed to evaluate
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Overall outcome that the protocol is designed to evaluate.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ act of signing up participants into a study
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Enrolling The act of signing up participants into a study.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ branch of medical science that deals with the study of incidence and distribution and control of a disease in a population
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Epidemiology The branch of medical science that deals with the study of incidence and distribution and control of a disease in a population.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ trial A trial with the primary objective of showing that the response to two or more treatments differs by an amount which is clinically unimportant
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Equivalence trial A trial with the primary objective of showing that the response to two or more treatments differs by an amount which is clinically unimportant. This is usually demonstrated by showing that the true treatment difference is likely to lie between a lower and an upper equivalence margin of clinically acceptable differences.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ that individually and collectively permit evaluation of the conduct of a study and the quality of the data produced
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Essential Documents Documents that individually and collectively permit evaluation of the conduct of a study and the quality of the data produced.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ disease Disease that cannot be measured directly by the size of the tumor but can be evaluated by other methods specific to a particular clinical trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Evaluable disease Disease that cannot be measured directly by the size of the tumor but can be evaluated by other methods specific to a particular clinical trial. (NCI) Evaluable patients Patients whose response to a treatment can be measured because enough information has been collected.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ patients Patients whose response to a treatment can be measured because enough information has been collected
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Evaluable disease Disease that cannot be measured directly by the size of the tumor but can be evaluated by other methods specific to a particular clinical trial. (NCI) Evaluable patients Patients whose response to a treatment can be measured because enough information has been collected.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ analysis set The set of subjects that is as close as possible to the ideal implied by the intention-to- treat principle
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Full analysis set The set of subjects that is as close as possible to the ideal implied by the intention-to- treat principle.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: The design of the study (such as a case report for an individual patient or a randomized double-blinded controlled clinical trial) and the endpoints measured (such as survival or _____) affect the strength of the evidence
Glossary of clinical research.fact: The design of the study (such as a case report for an individual patient or a randomized double-blinded controlled clinical trial) and the endpoints measured (such as survival or quality of life) affect the strength of the evidence.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ control subject An individual treated in the past and used in a comparison group when researchers analyze the results of a clinical study that had no control group
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Historical control subject An individual treated in the past and used in a comparison group when researchers analyze the results of a clinical study that had no control group.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ subject An individual who is or becomes a participant in research, either as a recipient of the test article or as a control
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Human subject An individual who is or becomes a participant in research, either as a recipient of the test article or as a control. A subject may be either a healthy human or a patient.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (21CFR50.3) _____ A supposition or assumption advanced as a basis for reasoning or argument, or as a guide to experimental investigation
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (21CFR50.3) Hypothesis A supposition or assumption advanced as a basis for reasoning or argument, or as a guide to experimental investigation.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ number of new cases of a disease diagnosed each year
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Incidence The number of new cases of a disease diagnosed each year.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____/exclusion criteria The medical or social standards determining whether a person may or may not be allowed to enter a clinical trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Inclusion/exclusion criteria The medical or social standards determining whether a person may or may not be allowed to enter a clinical trial. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are not used to reject people personally, but rather to identify appropriate participants and keep them safe.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ medicine, a sign, symptom, or medical condition that leads to the recommendation of a treatment, test, or procedure
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Indication In medicine, a sign, symptom, or medical condition that leads to the recommendation of a treatment, test, o.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ consent A process in which a person is given important facts about a medical procedure or treatment, a clinical trial, or genetic testing before deciding whether or not to participate
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Independent Ethics Committee An independent body (a review board or a committee, institutional, regional, national, or supranational), constituted of medical/scientific professionals and nonmedical/nonscientific members, whose responsibility it is to ensure the protection of the rights, safety, and well-being of human subjects involved in a trial and to provide public assurance of that protection, by, among other things, reviewing and approving/providing favorable opinion on the trial p...

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ public or private entity or agency or medical or dental facility where clinical trials are conducted
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Institution Any public or private entity or agency or medical or dental facility where clinical trials are conducted.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: There is an _____ at every health care facility that does clinical research
Glossary of clinical research.fact: There is an Institutional Review Board at every health care facility that does clinical research. Institutional Review Boards are designed to protect the people who take part in a clinical trial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (21CFR50.3) Intent to treat _____ of clinical trial results that includes all data from participants in the groups to which they were randomized even if they never received the treatment
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (21CFR50.3) Intent to treat Analysis of clinical trial results that includes all data from participants in the groups to which they were randomized even if they never received the treatment.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ (Qualitative & Quantitative) The situation in which a treatment contrast (e.g
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Interaction (Qualitative & Quantitative) The situation in which a treatment contrast (e.g. A quantitative interaction refers to the case where the magnitude of the contrast differs at the different levels of the factor, whereas for a qualitative interaction the direction of the contrast differs for at least one level of the factor.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____-rater reliability The property of yielding equivalent results when used by different raters on different occasions
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Interaction (Qualitative & Quantitative) The situation in which a treatment contrast (e.g. A quantitative interaction refers to the case where the magnitude of the contrast differs at the different levels of the factor, whereas for a qualitative interaction the direction of the contrast differs for at least one level of the factor.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ analysis Any analysis intended to compare treatment arms with respect to efficacy or safety at any time prior to the formal completion of a trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Interim analysis Any analysis intended to compare treatment arms with respect to efficacy or safety at any time prior to the formal completion of a trial. (ICH E9) Interim Clinical Trial/Study Report A report of intermediate results and their evaluation based on analyses performed during the course of a trial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____/Study Report A report of intermediate results and their evaluation based on analyses performed during the course of a trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Interim Clinical Trial/Study Report A report of intermediate results and their evaluation based on analyses performed during the course of a trial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ medicine, a treatment or action taken to prevent or treat disease, or improve health in other ways
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Intervention In medicine, a treatment or action taken to prevent or treat disease, or improve health in other ways.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ interventions being studied: types of interventions are Drug, Gene Transfer, Vaccine, Behavior, Device, or Procedure
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Primary interventions being studied: types of interventions are Drug, Gene Transfer, Vaccine, Behavior, Device, or Procedure.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ group The group receiving the study agent that is being tested in a clinical trial or clinical study
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Intervention In medicine, a treatment or action taken to prevent or treat disease, or improve health in other ways. (NCI) Primary interventions being studied: types of interventions are Drug, Gene Transfer, Vaccine, Behavior, Device, or Procedure.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ name The generic name of the precise intervention being studied
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Intervention In medicine, a treatment or action taken to prevent or treat disease, or improve health in other ways. (NCI) Primary interventions being studied: types of interventions are Drug, Gene Transfer, Vaccine, Behavior, Device, or Procedure.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____-rater reliability The property of yielding equivalent results when used by the same rater on different occasions
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Intra-rater reliability The property of yielding equivalent results when used by the same rater on different occasions.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ drug A substance that has been tested in a laboratory and has gotten approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to be tested in people
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Investigational In clinical trials, refers to a drug (including a new drug, dose, combination, or route of administration) or procedure that has undergone basic laboratory testing and received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to be tested in human subjects. A drug or procedure may be approved by the FDA for use in one disease or condition, but be considered investigational in other diseases or conditions.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ A new drug, antibiotic drug, or biological drug that is used in a clinical investigation
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Investigational New Drug A new drug, antibiotic drug, or biological drug that is used in a clinical investigation.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ A researcher in a clinical trial or clinical study
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Investigator A researcher in a clinical trial or clinical study. If a trial is conducted by a team of individuals at a trial site, the investigator is the responsible leader of the team and may be called the principal investigator.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (21CFR50.3) _____'s Brochure A compilation of the clinical and nonclinical data on the investigational product(s) that is relevant to the study of the investigational product(s) in human subjects
Glossary of clinical research.fact: If a trial is conducted by a team of individuals at a trial site, the investigator is the responsible leader of the team and may be called the principal investigator. (21CFR50.3) Investigator's Brochure A compilation of the clinical and nonclinical data on the investigational product(s) that is relevant to the study of the investigational product(s) in human subjects.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ of evidence A ranking system used to describe the strength of the results measured in a clinical trial or research study
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Levels of evidence A ranking system used to describe the strength of the results measured in a clinical trial or research study.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ tolerated dose The highest dose of a drug or treatment that does not cause unacceptable side effects
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Maximum tolerated dose The highest dose of a drug or treatment that does not cause unacceptable side effects. The maximum tolerated dose is determined in clinical trials by testing increasing doses on different groups of people until the highest dose with acceptable side effects is found.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ A legal drug that is used to prevent, treat, or relieve symptoms of a disease or abnormal condition
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Medication A legal drug that is used to prevent, treat, or relieve symptoms of a disease or abnormal condition.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ to the practices and procedures used for the prevention, treatment, or relief of symptoms of a diseases or abnormal conditions
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Medicine Refers to the practices and procedures used for the prevention, treatment, or relief of symptoms of a diseases or abnormal conditions.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____-analysis The formal evaluation of the quantitative evidence from two or more trials bearing on the same question
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Meta-analysis The formal evaluation of the quantitative evidence from two or more trials bearing on the same question.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ A written report from the monitor to the sponsor after each site visit and/or other trial-related communication according to the sponsor's SOPs
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Monitoring Report A written report from the monitor to the sponsor after each site visit and/or other trial-related communication according to the sponsor's SOPs.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ study A clinical trial that is carried out at more than one medical institution
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Multicenter study A clinical trial that is carried out at more than one medical institution.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ A large number or variety
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Multiplicity A large number or variety.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ history study A study that follows a group of people over time who have, or are at risk of developing, a specific medical condition or disease
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Natural history study A study that follows a group of people over time who have, or are at risk of developing, a specific medical condition or disease. A natural history study collects health information in order to understand how the medical condition or disease develops and how to treat it.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ of the natural development of something (such as an organism or a disease) over a period of time
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Natural history study A study that follows a group of people over time who have, or are at risk of developing, a specific medical condition or disease. A natural history study collects health information in order to understand how the medical condition or disease develops and how to treat it.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ (NDA) An application submitted by the manufacturer of a drug to the FDA - after clinical trials have been completed - for a license to market the drug for a specified indication
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) New Drug Application (NDA) An application submitted by the manufacturer of a drug to the FDA - after clinical trials have been completed - for a license to market the drug for a specified indication.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ a clinical trial or other experiment in which the researchers know what treatments are being given to each study subject or experimental group
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Nonblinded Describes a clinical trial or other experiment in which the researchers know what treatments are being given to each study subject or experimental group.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ studies not performed on human subjects
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Nonclinical Study Biomedical studies not performed on human subjects.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ case series A clinical study that includes some, but not all, of the eligible patients identified by the researchers during the study registration period
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Nonconsecutive case series A clinical study that includes some, but not all, of the eligible patients identified by the researchers during the study registration period.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ clinical trial A clinical trial in which the participants are not assigned by chance to different treatment groups
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Nonrandomized clinical trial A clinical trial in which the participants are not assigned by chance to different treatment groups.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ monitoring a patient's condition but withholding treatment until symptoms appear or change
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Observation Closely monitoring a patient's condition but withholding treatment until symptoms appear or change.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ study A type of study in which individuals are observed or certain outcomes are measured
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Observational study A type of study in which individuals are observed or certain outcomes are measured.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) Off-label _____ the legal use of a prescription drug to treat a disease or condition for which the drug has not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Off-label Describes the legal use of a prescription drug to treat a disease or condition for which the drug has not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ label study A type of study in which both the health providers and the patients are aware of the drug or treatment being given
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Open label study A type of study in which both the health providers and the patients are aware of the drug or treatment being given.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ drugs An FDA category that refers to medications used to treat diseases and conditions that occur rarely
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Orphan drugs An FDA category that refers to medications used to treat diseases and conditions that occur rarely. Orphan drug status, however, gives a manufacturer specific financial incentives to develop and provide such medications.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ A specific result or effect that can be measured
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Outcome A specific result or effect that can be measured. Examples of outcomes include decreased pain, reduced tumor size, and improvement of disease.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ A patient who visits a health care facility for diagnosis or treatment without spending the night
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Outpatient A patient who visits a health care facility for diagnosis or treatment without spending the night.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____-the-counter drug A medicine that can be bought without a prescription (doctor's order)
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Over-the-counter drug A medicine that can be bought without a prescription (doctor's order).

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) Peer review _____ of a clinical trial by experts chosen by the study sponsor
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Peer review Review of a clinical trial by experts chosen by the study sponsor. These experts review the trials for scientific merit, participant safety, and ethical considerations.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ processes (in a living organism) of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of a drug or vaccine
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Pharmacokinetics The processes (in a living organism) of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of a drug or vaccine.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ I clinical trials The first step in testing a new treatment in humans
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Phase I clinical trials The first step in testing a new treatment in humans. Because little is known about the possible risks and benefits of the treatments being tested, phase I trials usually include only a small number of patients who have not been helped by other treatments.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Because little is known about the possible risks and benefits of the treatments being tested, phase I trials usually include only a small number of patients who have not been helped by other treatments. (NLM) Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: During _____ 1, sufficient information about the drug's pharmacokinetics and pharmacological effects should be obtained to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans. Phase 1 studies are typically closely monitored and may be conducted in patients or normal volunteer subjects.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: The total number of subjects and patients included in _____ 1 studies varies with the drug, but is generally in the range of 20 to 80
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Phase 1 studies are typically closely monitored and may be conducted in patients or normal volunteer subjects. During Phase 1, sufficient information about the drug's pharmacokinetics and pharmacological effects should be obtained to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (21CFR312) _____ I/II trial A trial to study the safety, dosage levels, and response to a new treatment
Glossary of clinical research.fact: During Phase 1, sufficient information about the drug's pharmacokinetics and pharmacological effects should be obtained to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies. The total number of subjects and patients included in Phase 1 studies varies with the drug, but is generally in the range of 20 to 80.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (21CFR312) _____ II/III trial A trial to study response to a new treatment and the effectiveness of the treatment compared with the standard treatment regimen
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Phase II clinical trials A study to test whether a new treatment has an effect (NCI) Controlled clinical studies conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the drug for a particular indication or indications in patients with the disease or condition under study and to determine the common short-term side effects and risks. (NLM) Phase 2 includes the controlled clinical studies conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the drug for a particular indication or indications in patients with...

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ 3 studies are expanded controlled and uncontrolled trials
Glossary of clinical research.fact: In most cases, studies move into phase III only after a treatment seems to work in phases I and II. Phase III trials may include hundreds of people.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (21CFR312) _____ IV clinical trial After a treatment has been approved and is being marketed, it is studied in a phase IV trial to evaluate side effects that were not apparent in the phase III trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Phase 3 studies are expanded controlled and uncontrolled trials. Phase 3 studies usually include from several hundred to several thousand subjects.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____-marketing studies to delineate additional information including the drug's risks, benefits, and optimal use
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Post-marketing studies to delineate additional information including the drug's risks, benefits, and optimal use.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ study The initial study examining a new method or treatment
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Pilot study The initial study examining a new method or treatment.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ A placebo is an inactive pill, liquid, or powder that has no treatment value
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Placebo A placebo is an inactive pill, liquid, or powder that has no treatment value. In clinical trials, experimental treatments are often compared with placebos to assess the treatment's effectiveness.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ to a clinical study in which the control patients receive a placebo
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Refers to a clinical study in which the control patients receive a placebo.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ effect A physical or emotional change, occurring after a substance is taken or administered, that is not the result of any special property of the substance
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Placebo controlled study A method of investigation of drugs in which an inactive substance (the placebo) is given to one group of participants, while the drug being tested is given to another group. (NLM) Refers to a clinical study in which the control patients receive a placebo.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ therapy An inactive treatment or procedure that is intended to mimic as closely as possible a therapy in a clinical trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Refers to a clinical study in which the control patients receive a placebo. (NCI) Placebo effect A physical or emotional change, occurring after a substance is taken or administered, that is not the result of any special property of the substance.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ to the testing of experimental drugs in the test tube or in animals - the testing that occurs before trials in humans may be carried out
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Preclinical Refers to the testing of experimental drugs in the test tube or in animals - the testing that occurs before trials in humans may be carried out.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ factor A situation or condition that may increase a person's risk of developing a certain disease or disorder
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Predictive factor A situation or condition that may increase a person's risk of developing a certain disease or disorder.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ medicine, action taken to decrease the chance of getting a disease or condition
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Prevention In medicine, action taken to decrease the chance of getting a disease or condition.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ trials Refers to trials to find better ways to prevent disease in people who have never had the disease or to prevent a disease from returning
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Prevention In medicine, action taken to decrease the chance of getting a disease or condition. (NCI) Prevention trials Refers to trials to find better ways to prevent disease in people who have never had the disease or to prevent a disease from returning.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ to prevent disease
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Preventive Used to prevent disease.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ medicine, a study or clinical trial in which participants are identified and then followed forward in time
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Prospective In medicine, a study or clinical trial in which participants are identified and then followed forward in time.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: Throughout the ICH GCP _____, the term protocol refers to protocol and protocol amendments
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Throughout the ICH GCP Guidance, the term protocol refers to protocol and protocol amendments.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ A written description of a change(s) to or formal clarification of a protocol
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Throughout the ICH GCP Guidance, the term protocol refers to protocol and protocol amendments. (ICH E6) Protocol Amendment A written description of a change(s) to or formal clarification of a protocol.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ operational techniques and activities undertaken within the quality assurance system to verify that the requirements for quality of the trial related activities have been fulfilled
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Quality Control The operational techniques and activities undertaken within the quality assurance system to verify that the requirements for quality of the trial related activities have been fulfilled.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ of life trials (or supportive care trials) Refers to trials that explore ways to improve comfort and quality of life for individuals with a chronic illness
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Quality Control The operational techniques and activities undertaken within the quality assurance system to verify that the requirements for quality of the trial related activities have been fulfilled. (ICH E6) Quality of life trials (or supportive care trials) Refers to trials that explore ways to improve comfort and quality of life for individuals with a chronic illness.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ period during which a trial is attempting to identify and enroll participants
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Recruiting The period during which a trial is attempting to identify and enroll participants.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ A treatment plan that specifies the dosage, the schedule, and the duration of treatment
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Regimen A treatment plan that specifies the dosage, the schedule, and the duration of treatment.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ having the power to regulate
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Regulatory Authorities Bodies having the power to regulate.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: In the ICH GCP guidance, the expression "_____" includes the authorities that review submitted clinical data and those that conduct inspections
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Regulatory Authorities Bodies having the power to regulate. In the ICH GCP guidance, the expression "Regulatory Authorities" includes the authorities that review submitted clinical data and those that conduct inspections.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ back at events that have already taken place
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Retrospective Looking back at events that have already taken place.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____-benefit ratio The risk to individual participants versus the potential benefits
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Risk-benefit ratio The risk to individual participants versus the potential benefits. The risk/benefit ratio may differ depending on the condition being treated.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ trials Refers to trials which test the best way to detect certain diseases or health conditions
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Screening trials Refers to trials which test the best way to detect certain diseases or health conditions.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ bias An error in choosing the individuals or groups to take part in a study
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Selection bias An error in choosing the individuals or groups to take part in a study.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ therapy An inactive treatment or procedure that is intended to mimic as closely as possible a therapy in a clinical trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Sham therapy An inactive treatment or procedure that is intended to mimic as closely as possible a therapy in a clinical trial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ effect A problem that occurs when treatment affects healthy tissues or organs
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Side effect A problem that occurs when treatment affects healthy tissues or organs. Experimental drugs must be evaluated for both immediate and long-term side effects (NLM) Significant In statistics, describes a mathematical measure of difference between groups.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: Experimental drugs must be evaluated for both immediate and long-term side effects (NLM) _____ statistics, describes a mathematical measure of difference between groups
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Experimental drugs must be evaluated for both immediate and long-term side effects (NLM) Significant In statistics, describes a mathematical measure of difference between groups.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NCI) _____ blind study A type of clinical trial in which only the doctor knows whether a patient is taking the standard treatment or the new treatment being tested
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NCI) Single blind study A type of clinical trial in which only the doctor knows whether a patient is taking the standard treatment or the new treatment being tested. (NCI) A study in which one party, either the investigator or participant, is unaware of what medication the participant is taking; also called single-masked study.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ individual, company, institution, or organization that takes responsibility for the initiation, management, and/or financing of a clinical trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Sponsor An individual, company, institution, or organization that takes responsibility for the initiation, management, and/or financing of a clinical trial.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (21CFR50.3) _____ treatment A treatment currently in wide use and approved by the FDA, considered to be effective in the treatment of a specific disease or condition
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (21CFR50.3) Standard treatment A treatment currently in wide use and approved by the FDA, considered to be effective in the treatment of a specific disease or condition. (NLM) Standards of care Treatment regimen or medical management based on state of the art participant care.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ of care Treatment regimen or medical management based on state of the art participant care
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Standards of care Treatment regimen or medical management based on state of the art participant care.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____, written instructions to achieve uniformity of the performance of a specific function
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Standard Operating Procedures Detailed, written instructions to achieve uniformity of the performance of a specific function.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ significance The probability that an event or difference occurred by chance alone
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Statistical analysis plan A statistical analysis plan is a document that contains a more technical and detailed elaboration of the principal features of the analysis described in the protocol, and includes detailed procedures for executing the statistical analysis of the primary and secondary variables and other data. (ICH E9) Statistical significance The probability that an event or difference occurred by chance alone.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ endpoint A primary or secondary outcome used to judge the effectiveness of a treatment
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Study endpoint A primary or secondary outcome used to judge the effectiveness of a treatment. (NLM) Study type The primary investigative techniques used in an observational protocol; types are Purpose, Duration, Selection, and Timing.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) Study type The primary investigative techniques used in an observational protocol; types are _____, Duration, Selection, and Timing
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Study type The primary investigative techniques used in an observational protocol; types are Purpose, Duration, Selection, and Timing.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) Subject/_____ individual who participates in a clinical trial, either as a recipient of the investigational product(s) or as a control
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Subject/Trial Subject An individual who participates in a clinical trial, either as a recipient of the investigational product(s) or as a control.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E6) _____ trial A trial with the primary objective of showing that the response to the investigational product is superior to a comparative agent (active or placebo control)
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E6) Superiority trial A trial with the primary objective of showing that the response to the investigational product is superior to a comparative agent (active or placebo control).

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ variable A variable that provides an indirect measurement of effect in situations where direct measurement of clinical effect is not feasible or practical
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Surrogate variable A variable that provides an indirect measurement of effect in situations where direct measurement of clinical effect is not feasible or practical.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ effect An effect attributed to a treatment in a clinical trial
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Treatment effect An effect attributed to a treatment in a clinical trial. In most clinical trials the treatment effect of interest is a comparison (or contrast) of two or more treatments.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (ICH E9) _____ emergent An event that emerges during treatment having been absent pre-treatment, or worsens relative to the pre-treatment state
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Treatment effect An effect attributed to a treatment in a clinical trial. In most clinical trials the treatment effect of interest is a comparison (or contrast) of two or more treatments.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: Treatment INDs are made available to participants before general marketing begins, typically during _____ III studies
Glossary of clinical research.fact: Treatment INDs are made available to participants before general marketing begins, typically during Phase III studies.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ trials Refers to trials which test new treatments, new combinations of drugs, or new approaches to surgery or radiation therapy
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (ICH E9) Treatment IND IND stands for Investigational New Drug application, which is part of the process to get approval from the FDA for marketing a new prescription drug in the U.S. It makes promising new drugs available to desperately ill participants as early in the drug development process as possible. Treatment INDs are made available to participants before general marketing begins, typically during Phase III studies.

Glossary of clinical research.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of clinical research.question: (NLM) _____ location(s) where trial-related activities are actually conducted
Glossary of clinical research.fact: (NLM) Trial Site The location(s) where trial-related activities are actually conducted.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Has largely been replaced by _____ since the mid 2000s
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Has largely been replaced by PCI Express since the mid 2000s.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: accelerator A microprocessor, _____, or expansion card designed to offload a specific task from the CPU, often containing fixed-function hardware
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: accelerator A microprocessor, ASIC, or expansion card designed to offload a specific task from the CPU, often containing fixed-function hardware.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Advanced Technology eXtended (ATX) A motherboard form factor specification developed by Intel in _____ to improve on previous DE factor standards like the AT form factor
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Advanced Technology eXtended (ATX) A motherboard form factor specification developed by Intel in 1995 to improve on previous DE factor standards like the AT form factor.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Advanced Configuration and _____ open standard for operating systems to discover, configure, manage, and monitor status of the hardware
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Advanced Configuration and Power Interface An open standard for operating systems to discover, configure, manage, and monitor status of the hardware.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Blu-ray _____ is capable of storing about 5 times as much data as a standard DVD
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Advanced Configuration and Power Interface An open standard for operating systems to discover, configure, manage, and monitor status of the hardware. Blu-ray Disc is capable of storing about 5 times as much data as a standard DVD.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: cache eviction _____ up data from within a cache to make room for new cache entries to be allocated; controlled by a cache replacement policy
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: cache eviction Freeing up data from within a cache to make room for new cache entries to be allocated; controlled by a cache replacement policy.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: cache hit _____ data in a local cache, preventing the need to search for that resource in a more distant location (or to repeat a calculation)
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: cache hit Finding data in a local cache, preventing the need to search for that resource in a more distant location (or to repeat a calculation). cache miss Not finding data in a local cache, requiring use of the cache policy to allocate and fill this data, and possibly performing evicting other data to make room.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: cache-only memory architecture (_____) A multiprocessor memory architecture where an address space is dynamically shifted between processor nodes based on demand
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: cache-only memory architecture (COMA) A multiprocessor memory architecture where an address space is dynamically shifted between processor nodes based on demand.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: device memory local memory associated with a hardware device such as a graphics processing unit or _____CL compute device, distinct from main memory
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: device memory local memory associated with a hardware device such as a graphics processing unit or OpenCL compute device, distinct from main memory.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Primarily used for storing movies and computer games, however, the rise of services such as _____ have largely rendered physical game discs obsolete
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Primarily used for storing movies and computer games, however, the rise of services such as Steam have largely rendered physical game discs obsolete.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Digital Visual Interface (DVI) A video display interface developed by the _____ (DDWG)
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Digital Visual Interface (DVI) A video display interface developed by the Digital Display Working Group (DDWG).

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Unlike HDMI, _____Port is open source
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: DisplayPort A digital display interface developed by the Video Electronics Standards Association (VESA). The interface is primarily used to connect a video source to a display device such as a computer monitor, though it can also be used to transmit audio, USB, and other forms of data.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: dual in-line memory module (_____) A series of dynamic random-access memory integrated circuits
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: dual in-line memory module (DIMM) A series of dynamic random-access memory integrated circuits.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: firmware _____ programs and data that internally control various electronic devices
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: firmware Fixed programs and data that internally control various electronic devices.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: These were common on computers made prior to _____
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: These were common on computers made prior to 2010.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: High-_____ (HDMI) A compact interface for transferring encrypted uncompressed digital audio and video data to a device such as a computer monitor, video projector or digital television
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: High-Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI) A compact interface for transferring encrypted uncompressed digital audio and video data to a device such as a computer monitor, video projector or digital television.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Motherboard and graphics card manufacturers must pay a licensing fee to incorporate _____ into their products
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: High-Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI) A compact interface for transferring encrypted uncompressed digital audio and video data to a device such as a computer monitor, video projector or digital television. Motherboard and graphics card manufacturers must pay a licensing fee to incorporate HDMI into their products.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Input/_____ (IOPS) A common performance measurement used to benchmark computer storage devices like hard disk drives
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Input/Output Operations Per Second (IOPS) A common performance measurement used to benchmark computer storage devices like hard disk drives.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: a cache, scratchpad, the memory connected to one processor node in a _____ or COMA system, or device memory (such as VRAM) in an accelerator
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: a cache, scratchpad, the memory connected to one processor node in a NUMA or COMA system, or device memory (such as VRAM) in an accelerator.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Main memory usually consists of _____, and is distinct from caches and scratchpads
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Main memory usually consists of DRAM, and is distinct from caches and scratchpads.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: memory _____ that are used to store data or programs on a temporary or permanent basis for use in an electronic digital computer
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: memory Devices that are used to store data or programs on a temporary or permanent basis for use in an electronic digital computer.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: by _____ or wireless networking
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: by Ethernet or wireless networking.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: non-uniform memory access (_____) non-volatile memory memory that can retain the stored data even when not powered, as opposed to volatile memory
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: non-uniform memory access (NUMA) non-volatile memory memory that can retain the stored data even when not powered, as opposed to volatile memory.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: non-volatile random-access memory _____-access memory (RAM) that retains its data when power is turned off
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: non-volatile random-access memory Random-access memory (RAM) that retains its data when power is turned off.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: operation code _____ bits in a computer program instruction that specify which operation to perform
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: operation code Several bits in a computer program instruction that specify which operation to perform.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: pentest _____ name for a penetration test
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: pentest Another name for a penetration test.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: power supply unit (PSU) _____ mains AC to low-voltage regulated DC power for the internal components of a computer
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: power supply A unit of the computer that converts mains AC to low-voltage regulated DC for the power of all the computer components. power supply unit (PSU) Converts mains AC to low-voltage regulated DC power for the internal components of a computer.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: process node _____ to a level of semiconductor manufacturing technology, one of several successive transistor shrinks
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: process node Refers to a level of semiconductor manufacturing technology, one of several successive transistor shrinks.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: programmable read-only memory (_____) A type of non-volatile memory chip that may be programmed after the device is constructed
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: programmable read-only memory (PROM) A type of non-volatile memory chip that may be programmed after the device is constructed. programmer Any electronic equipment that arranges written software to configure programmable non-volatile integrated circuits (called programmable devices) such as EPROMs, EEPROMs, Flashes, eMMC, MRAM, FRAM, NV RAM, PALs, FPGAs or programmable logic circuits.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: PCI _____ (PCIe) An expansion bus standard designed to replace the older PCI, PCI-X, and AGP bus standards
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: PCI Express (PCIe) An expansion bus standard designed to replace the older PCI, PCI-X, and AGP bus standards.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: PCI-e_____ (PCI-X) An expansion bus and expansion card standard that enhances the 32-bit PCI Local Bus for higher bandwidth demanded by servers
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: PCI-eXtended (PCI-X) An expansion bus and expansion card standard that enhances the 32-bit PCI Local Bus for higher bandwidth demanded by servers.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: single in-line memory module (_____) A type of memory module containing random-access memory used in computers from the early 1980s to the late 1990s
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: single in-line memory module (SIMM) A type of memory module containing random-access memory used in computers from the early 1980s to the late 1990s.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: static random-access memory (_____) A type of semiconductor memory that uses bistable latching circuitry to store each bit
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: static random-access memory (SRAM) A type of semiconductor memory that uses bistable latching circuitry to store each bit.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: The term static differentiates it from _____, which must be periodically refreshed
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: The term static differentiates it from DRAM, which must be periodically refreshed. storage device synchronous dynamic random-access memory (SDRAM) A type of dynamic random access memory that is synchronized with the system bus.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: storage device synchronous dynamic random-access memory (_____) A type of dynamic random access memory that is synchronized with the system bus
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: storage device synchronous dynamic random-access memory (SDRAM) A type of dynamic random access memory that is synchronized with the system bus.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: The SuperDisk hardware was created by 3M's storage products group Imation in _____
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: The SuperDisk hardware was created by 3M's storage products group Imation in 1997.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: Serial ATA (SATA) _____ AT Attachment
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: Serial ATA (SATA) Also Serial AT Attachment.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: It can also be used to connect devices such as video game consoles, videocassette recorders, and _____Disc players, if necessary
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: It can also be used to connect devices such as video game consoles, videocassette recorders, and LaserDisc players, if necessary.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: The USB standard was first finalized in _____, and has undergone many revisions since then, enabling faster data transfer speeds
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: The USB standard was first finalized in 1996, and has undergone many revisions since then, enabling faster data transfer speeds.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: uop cache A cache of decoded micro-operations in a _____ processor (e.g x86)
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: uop cache A cache of decoded micro-operations in a CISC processor (e.g x86).

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: USB 1.x The first revision of USB, which was capable of transferring up to 12 _____/s (megabits per second)
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: USB 1.x The first revision of USB, which was capable of transferring up to 12 Mbit/s (megabits per second). It significantly increased the maximum transfer rate to 480 Mbit/s.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: It significantly increased the maximum transfer rate to 480 _____/s
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: USB 1.x The first revision of USB, which was capable of transferring up to 12 Mbit/s (megabits per second). It significantly increased the maximum transfer rate to 480 Mbit/s.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: USB 2.0 The second revision of USB, introduced in _____
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: USB 2.0 The second revision of USB, introduced in 2000.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: USB 3.0 The third revision of USB, introduced in _____
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: USB 3.0 The third revision of USB, introduced in 2008.

Glossary of computer hardware terms.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of computer hardware terms.question: It provides transfer rates of up to 5 _____/s (gigabits per second), more than 10 times faster than USB 2.0
Glossary of computer hardware terms.fact: It provides transfer rates of up to 5 Gbit/s (gigabits per second), more than 10 times faster than USB 2.0.

Glossary of ecology.subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of ecology.question: greenhouse effect The warming of the _____'s climate that results from solar irradiance being trapped in the atmosphere
Glossary of ecology.fact: greenhouse effect The warming of the Earth's climate that results from solar irradiance being trapped in the atmosphere. The phenomenon is caused by atmospheric gases which allow the sun's energy to reach the Earth's surface but subsequently absorb heat that is radiated back from the warmed surface.
